title: Snipe Guide — Charge Stages, Perfect Window and Bow Marksman
summary: Snipe is a bow channel skill: holding to aim accumulates stages that raise damage and crit, and at full charge it opens a brief 'perfect' release window granting extra crit and damage. This guide explains how stages build, why the perfect window is hard to catch, the cost of releasing too early or too late, how it splits duties with Ice Shot / Lightning Arrow, and why it fits Deadeye's ranged single-target play.
description: Snipe deep guide: charge stages and damage / crit curve, perfect window mechanic, comparison with Ice Shot / Lightning Arrow, recommended crit / attack-speed / damage supports, Deadeye role, mis-timed release and lost-charge causes with direct answers, video timestamps and real community questions.
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial

sections.title: Overview: Aim → Charge → Perfect Shot
paragraphs: Snipe is a bow channel skill: you hold to enter an aim state, and the arrow's damage and crit rise with charge stages; once fully charged it opens a brief 'perfect' window where releasing fires an arrow with extra crit and damage. It is not a mindless 'hold forever' skill — it is a rhythm-based single-target burst about catching the perfect window.

Its core value is ranged single-target: unlike mobile attacks like Ice Shot / Lightning Arrow, Snipe trades mobility for one extremely heavy hit — ideal for safely grinding a boss from range or deleting high-threat targets you can't facetank. The cost is that you must stand and aim; being interrupted, knocked back, or moving loses the charge.

This is why Deadeye ranged builds love it: Deadeye's far-distance, crit and pierce ascendancies amplify a 'perfect Snipe' payoff, and with far-shot-style mechanics it can produce absurd single-target numbers.
bullets: Essence: bow channel skill, stages raise damage / crit, full charge has a perfect window.
Role: ranged single-target burst, trades mobility for one heavy hit.
Risk: interrupted / knockback / moving during aim loses the charge.
Common carrier: Deadeye ranged single-target builds.

sections.title: Mechanics: How Stages Build, How to Catch the Window
paragraphs: Stage buildup: while holding to aim, Snipe accumulates stages over time; higher stages mean more damage and crit on that shot. So even without chasing perfect, a full charge is far stronger than zero charge — charging itself is the main damage source.

Perfect window: when stages reach near-max, a very short 'perfect' window opens. Releasing inside it grants extra crit and damage (often including guaranteed-crit or crit bonuses). The window is tiny, so you must practice the feel of 'release at the moment of full charge' — too early and it's not full, too late and the window passed.

Release timing cost: releasing too early (stages not full) sacrifices most damage; releasing too late (perfect window passed, still outside full) is just a normal full charge, missing the extra crit. Many players agonize over 'should I wait for perfect' — the answer is usually: wait if you can catch it reliably; for kite fights or when rushed, fire at full charge.
bullets: Charging itself is the main damage; full charge >> zero charge.
Perfect window near full charge: extra crit + damage, very short.
Too early loses damage, too late misses the extra crit.
Catch perfect if stable; mobile fights fire at full charge.

rows: Emergency or interrupted fire; lowest damage
Stable single-target, most common release point
Catch it if you can — single-target peak

sections.title: Comparison: Snipe vs Ice Shot / Lightning Arrow
paragraphs: Snipe is 'stand and snipe'; Ice Shot / Lightning Arrow are 'move and fire'. The former has the highest single-target peak but sacrifices mobility; the latter sustain movement DPS and clearing. A mature Deadeye often lets Snipe handle bosses you can't facetank while Ice Shot / Lightning Arrow handle kiting clear andfiller damage.

Cadence difference: Snipe's effective DPS hinges on whether you can stand and charge and catch perfect; once frequently interrupted, its effective DPS collapses. Ice Shot-style skills are almost interruption-immune. So Snipe's strength is half positioning / interrupt resistance, half numbers.

Shared system: all three use bow and attack speed. Snipe's charge time is unrelated to attack speed (charge follows a fixed rhythm), but attack speed affects the gap between two Snipes. Don't treat 'attack speed speeds up Snipe charge' as fact when gearing.
bullets: Snipe stands and snipes, highest ST peak; Ice Shot / LA move and fire.
Snipe's effective DPS is extremely dependent on standing and interrupt resist.
Attack speed does not speed Snipe charge, only the gap between shots.

supports.label: Critical Damage / Crit supports
notes: Snipe already stacks crit; crit-damage supports directly amplify the perfect-window burst.
Best stacked with ensured-crit / crit-bonus mechanics.

supports.label: Damage supports (by damage type)
notes: If you run physical / elemental hybrid, the matching damage support lifts each shot's base.
Pick by your actual damage type; don't blind-slot.

supports.label: Bloodthirst / full-life damage
notes: Snipe often stands and outputs without losing life, so full-life damage supports stay maxed.
Fits stationary builds that aren't frequently chipped.

supports.label: Greater Multiple Projectiles
notes: Snipe usually goes single-target; multi-proj splits ST and ruins the sniper feel, generally avoided.
Only consider for a deliberate 'charged scatter' tech.

supports.label: Martial Tempo / Attack Speed
notes: Doesn't speed charging but shortens the gap between two Snipes, raising effective DPS.
Clearly useful when you get many stand-and-fire openings.

supports.label: Execute (if available)
notes: Extra damage to low-life targets, pairs with Snipe's single-target burst for finishers.
Confirm current client maps it onto attacks.

sections.title: Role in Builds
paragraphs: Deadeye ranged single-target: the most typical carrier. Far-distance and crit ascendancies amplify the perfect Snipe as a boss / high-threat finisher, while cold / lightning attacks handle kiting clear.
Frost-bow secondary sniper: primary Ice Shot clears, switch to Snipe for unfreezable or reliably-single-target situations. They share a bow, so swapping is cheap — a common dual-bow setup.

Interrupt resistance is a prerequisite: any map that frequently knocks you back or force-displaces (breaking Snipe's charge) craters its effective DPS. In those scenes Ice Shot / Lightning Arrow sustained output beats Snipe.
bullets: Deadeye: perfect Snipe as boss finisher, cold / lightning for clear.
Frost bow: Snipe as ST secondary when ailments fail.
Maps with heavy knockback / forced displacement — Snipe loses to sustained skills.

sections.title: Common Mistakes: Lost Charge / Missed Perfect
paragraphs: Charge keeps breaking: you stand where knockback, forced displacement, or melee interrupts happen. Direct answer: create distance, use terrain for line-of-sight, and prioritize interrupt resistance / stand-your-ground before practicing Snipe.

Can't catch the perfect window: the window is tiny and the feel isn't built yet. Direct answer: first practice 'release at full charge' on a dummy; once stable, try catching perfect; in rushed fights just fire at full charge, don't force it.

Thinking attack speed speeds charging: Snipe charge follows a fixed rhythm; attack speed only affects the gap between shots. Direct answer: don't stack attack speed to 'charge faster' — its value is in cadence, not charging.
Using Snipe as a clear skill: it has high single-target peak but weak AoE and needs standing. Direct answer: leave clearing to Ice Shot / Lightning Arrow; Snipe focuses single-target.
bullets: Issue: charge keeps breaking.
Direct answer: distance + terrain + interrupt resist, then practice Snipe.
Issue: can't catch the perfect window.
Direct answer: practice full-charge release first, then perfect.
Issue: mistakenly think attack speed speeds charging.
Direct answer: attack speed only affects shot cadence, not charge.

items.question: Do I have to wait for the perfect window?
answer: No. Full charge (non-perfect) is already near-cap output; perfect is just extra crit + damage.
Catch it if stable; for kite fights or when rushed, fire at full charge, don't force perfect.

items.question: Does attack speed make me charge faster?
answer: No. Snipe charge follows a fixed rhythm; attack speed only affects the gap between shots.
To raise effective DPS, prioritize stable standing and interrupt resistance.

items.question: Why does my Snipe keep getting interrupted?
answer: Standing too close gets you meleed, or the map has heavy knockback / forced displacement.
Direct answer: create distance, use terrain, and stack interrupt resistance / stand-your-ground.
